title: SNAP Loses 4 Million Participants Steepest Drop in 30 Years Under Big Beautiful Bill
description_short: SNAP Loses 4 Million Participants Steepest Drop in 30 Years Under Big Beautiful Bill
description_medium: More than 4 million Americans lost SNAP food assistance between July 2025 and March 2026, the steepest six-month decline since 1997, following HR 1 187 billion in SNAP cuts. The law expanded work requirements to adults ages 55-64, raised paperwork burdens, and for the first time required states to fund a share of SNAP benefits. Harvard public health professor Sara Naomi Bleich confirmed the drop reflects policy changes, not economic improvement, as unemployment remained flat.
description_long: The supplied account says more than 4 million Americans stopped receiving SNAP food assistance between July 2025 and March 2026 following H.R. 1's $187 billion in program cuts. The law expanded work requirements to adults aged 55 to 64, increased paperwork demands and required states to pay a share of benefit costs for the first time. These provisions describe mechanisms that can change access to assistance, distinct from the separate enrollment figure. Harvard public-health professor Sara Naomi Bleich attributed the decline to policy changes rather than an improving economy, noting that unemployment remained flat. That causal assessment should remain attributed to her. The synopsis also labels the July-to-March period a six-month decline, although the dates span longer; the new explanation preserves the dates without repeating that inconsistent characterization. The event records the scale of the reported loss and the policy changes associated with it. It does not establish that every departing household left for the same reason.
